column1: # Recent happenings for the report: changes that are not test results (those are added from the grades automatically).
# when (local, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM)<TAB>kind (queue | model | engine | settings | tests | grading | finding)<TAB>one or two plain sentences.
# Newest first by convention; the report sorts by time. Add a line whenever the queue, a model, a setting, a test or a grader changes.

column3: The ten uncensored orreries are all status ok and that queue finished at 08:18. Tiel pagoda pilot round 2 finished status ok and is not graded; the orrery pilot is running. Not ALL DONE.
Gated repos accepted by the operator: official PersonaPlex-7B weights and orcarouter's own vision heads downloaded and verified; the orcarouter Flash-Next vision entry now uses its own head.

Grok review applied: the new-work slot now unloads and releases the lease when stopped, keeps failed steps apart, and every later queue names it in its wait list; the SVG renderer gives no frame if its loopback server is down.

Operator decisions: Cyber stays in the tests; test 8 is for vision feedback, so scored test 8 waits for vision entries; vision heads for every catalog model; all six Iris engines; LFM2.5 test 2 queued in a new queue slot (bakeoff-queue-new) before redo-big; the SVG renderer serves over loopback http instead of file://.

Tiel pilot reviewed (pagoda 7, orrery 3, test 7 auto 0: generator worked but no ./generate at the cap). Round 3: /fit without temp files and with failure logging; test 7 preamble says work is graded as it stands at the cap. Pilot round 2 (p2 pagoda, orrery, test 7) queued after the uncensored orreries.

Test 8 tuning round 2 (Grok-reviewed): pilot no longer waits for uncensored (deadlock), bash timeout 5 min (test 8) / 9 min (test 7), preview failures are harness failures, /fit bounded, watchdog test. Tiel pagoda pilot graded 7.

Test 8 tuning from the tiel pilot: the preview reachable from the agent's shell (port taken), the SVG view as the grader shows it, prompt wording, hang watchdog ignores harness processes; tests/test_test8.sh ALL PASS.
Ten uncensored pagodas graded: qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-vllm 9, cyber-tiel-coder-35b 9, orcasaq2-cyber-27b 7, flashnext-heretic2 5, six blank from script errors.
Tiel pilot moved ahead of the uncensored orreries (operator: tiel next, finish uncensored overnight); pagodas done, rendered and graded.

Three more uncensored pagoda one-shots finished status ok (Cyber Q5 33.4 tok/s, Cyber Tiel 47.6 tok/s, Flash-Next Heretic2 13.7 tok/s). Flash-Next abliterated s1.5 is loading. Eight of ten pagodas are done; the orreries and the tiel pilot are still waiting.
Pilot wiring Grok-reviewed: queue defaults now carry the hold, the pilot unit fails if a child fails, idle waits for pilot and hold, check text clarified.
Tiel agentic pilot queued after the uncensored one-shots: test 8 pagoda and orrery, then test 7 (-p1 cases); redo-big next; full test 8/7 held until tuned.
Test 5 graded from re-rendered frames: tiel t06 run 4 10/10, tiel q4kxl 9, HyperQwen 0.31 9; HyperQwen pagoda 0 (blank).
SVG frames now seek to their time (iframe without scripts + pauseAnimations/setCurrentTime); before, every orrery frame was the first one.

HyperQwen vLLM 0.31 timed rounds match 0.30 on short tasks (code about 124 vs 126 tok/s, prose 93 vs 91, structured 135 to 137). The 141k needle passed both ways. Deep code is a little slower on 0.31 (79.5 vs 84.5 tok/s). The warm-up round is not compared.

The HyperQwen trial's speed rounds finished at 21:15 with no failures. Its pagoda one-shot finished status ok (95.4 tok/s, 9 min) and is not graded here. The orrery one-shot is running. The later queues are still waiting.
Recreated the hourly bake-off check for the live queue chain; the three-hourly grading reminder is gone.
Fill to five was parked by hand after its park script stuck on a zombie process. The HyperQwen vLLM 0.31 trial started at 20:47.
Recreated the daily 11:00 Iris check automation, now owned by the Model Master 2 conversation.

Gemma own-server test 3 run 5 is graded: rubric 8/12, 14/14 facts, 2.4 tok/s over 68 min. It fixed list_entities (HashMap to Vec) so tool_call passes. Init still fails, and the probe never called a tool.
Fill-to-five's park script is stuck on a zombie of the finished Gemma case, so the queue has not stopped and the HyperQwen trial has not started.
Review-site publisher hardened after the late pivot review (symlinked meta/frames skipped, bad meta.json drops one case, three addons paths).
Queued a HyperQwen vLLM 0.31 trial: speed bench against 0.30, then pagoda and orrery one-shots; runs before the uncensored one-shots.
Tiel Coder test 2 run 5 is a full pass: 26 tests, 80.4 tok/s, 15 min. Gemma test 3 runs 2 to 4 are graded. The known-good server was really checked on three runs.

Four Gemma test 3 runs wrote a 14/14 facts file without an MCP tool call. Three sent the brief to explore or general instead of mcp-probe. One own-server run started 17 probes and then said it simulated them.
Pivot: repeat runs (fill to five, runs 2-5) become idle-time work; uncensored one-shots, then test 8 run 1 with the uncensored models first.
Review site: one table per task, one-shot (blind) and agent + browser (verified) rows side by side.
Added the Cyber Q5 author quant to the uncensored one-shots (ten models now).
Queued the one-shot pagoda and orrery for nine uncensored models, after the full-context redo and before test 8.
Test 8 now alternates which task runs first, and stops a case instead of turning screenshots off when the image check gets no answer from the server.

Queued test 8 after the running queues: the pagoda and the orrery as agent tasks for five models, five runs each. The agent may start sub-agents and has a sealed browser to look at its own page, but no Internet; the file it leaves is graded like the one-shots.
At 18:41 I unloaded the model under wb-tiel-t06-r5 by mistake (a check of llama-swap's admin page). It lost one step and reloaded; the case is flagged and will be rerun if its result looks affected.

Agents now get a larger working window before they compact. The limit had counted the 32k reply twice. So Qwen (150k) compacted at 71k; it now compacts at 89k. The 262k models move from 172k to 201k. Runs from now on use the new window. Earlier runs, including all of test 2, used the old one.

Queued a redo of pagoda (test 6) and orrery (test 5) for seven models, once the running queues end. Each model gets a reply cap near its full context (90k-140k instead of 32k) and up to 10 hours. Up to three tries per model, with a thinking-off fallback, so each one ends with a page and an orrery. It replaces the 96k pagoda queue.

Posted our RTX 3090 TensorFold 0.6.6 + DFlash2 numbers on upstream issue #603, as a receipt for their 3090 port, with the operator's OK on the exact text. Next is a native build to try when they publish one.

Gemma test 2 runs 4 and 5 are graded and archived and are not full passes. Run 4 fails the handshake and its tool calls, and its tests hang (131 min, 12 tok/s). Run 5 shakes hands, then sends the method name as the tool name (4 tests, 2 min, 134 tok/s). Qwen3.8-27B vLLM runs 2 and 3 are full passes: 40 tests in 34 min at 73 tok/s, and 32 tests in 25 min at 75 tok/s. One grep call returned a match. Public cards are agentic-toolbox PR 87.
The review page now sorts in place when you click a column header, and Esc closes pop-ups. Its one script is allowed only on the index pages.
Pagoda round with a 96k reply cap queued for the three setups that got cut off (9 runs). The review site now publishes when a queue finishes instead of on a timer.
The review page's text columns now sort with numbers in names in order (run 2 before run 10); number columns already sorted by value.

Tiel t06 test 1 run 5 is graded and archived: 5/5, 42 tests, 7 subcommands, 45 min, 30 tok/s. The read probe showed 416 fixture entities. Gemma test 2 run 2 is a thin full pass (3 tools, 3 tests, 4 min, 154 tok/s) and its glob call returned files. Run 3 fails initialize because the reply uses snake_case field names; the primary tool still returned data. Public cards are agentic-toolbox PR 86.
The review page now sorts by any column, shows each run's context size, reply cap and thinking, and opens settings, specs and enlarged frames as pop-ups on the same page.
Test 7's grader now runs each unseen seed in its own sealed container and refuses to grade a case that never ran; the runner and queue got safer exits. No test 7 case has run yet.

Tiel t06 test 1 run 4 is graded and archived: 5/5, 38 tests, 18 subcommands, 13 min, 88 tok/s. The read probe showed 329 fixture entities. No glob or grep calls, and no ownership error. Run 5 is still going. The public card row is agentic-toolbox PR 85.
Test 7 added: each model writes a generator for a three-floor labyrinth that must pass a ten-rule checker, on seeds it has not seen; the best mazes will be built in Minecraft.

Qwen3.8-27B vLLM test 1 run 5 and Tiel t06 test 1 runs 2 and 3 are graded and archived. Qwen run 5 is 5/5 with 114 tests in 25 min at 76 tok/s. Tiel run 2 is 5/5 with 33 tests in 9 min at 106 tok/s. Tiel run 3 is 2/5: reads, bad input and bad auth fail, while 39 tests pass, in 12 min at 96 tok/s. Run 4 just started.
Qwen3.8-27B vLLM test 1 runs 3 and 4 are graded and archived. Both are 5/5: run 3 has 67 tests in 52 min at 70 tok/s, run 4 has 68 tests in 16 min at 73 tok/s. Run 5 is going.

Graded 15 fill-to-five pagodas. Tiel t06 runs 4 and 5 both scored 10. Gemma scored 9 and 8, with flat eaves. Qwen3.8-27B vLLM thinking-on runs 1 to 5 are one byte-identical cut-off and score 0. ExLlamaV3 with thinking off scored DFlash2 6, 8, 0 and MTP 0, 0, 0.

Gemma test 1 runs 2 to 5 are graded and archived. Run 2 is 5/5 checks, 9 pass and 1 fail, 167 tok/s. Run 3 is 3/5: bad input and bad auth fail, 8 tests pass, 143 tok/s. Run 4 is 5/5, 6 tests, 125 tok/s. Run 5 is 4/5 because no_crash failed, 5 tests, 102 tok/s.
Fill-to-five finished the pagoda and orrery one-shots and their renders, then started the agent tests. Gemma test 1 is done. Qwen3.8-27B vLLM test 1 run 3 is loaded. Flash is still waiting.

Fill-to-five took the lease at 07:46. Qwen3.8-27B vLLM wrote no voxel pagoda in five tries (each about 6 min, about 95 tok/s, cut off at the length cap). Tiel t06 and Gemma runs 4 and 5 did write pages, thinking-off exllamav3 MTP wrote three, and DFlash2 wrote two with the third started at 08:33. Not graded here. Phase-d was not restarted.
Unit bakeoff-queue-five is running the thinking-off exllamav3 pagodas. Orrery one-shots and the agent tests are still ahead. Flash is waiting and has not loaded.

Public model-research card updated (agentic-toolbox PR 81): test 6 pagoda in method and cards, ExLlamaV3 and TensorFold engine notes, Tiel and Gemma daily drivers; Grok review fixes applied (sample counts, Tiel failures, five vLLM tries).
Flash-Next's fill-to-five now runs on the SGLang phase-d build (flashnext-phased), test 3 included: it serves several sessions at once, which the older SGLang build could not.

Qwen3.8-27B on exllamav3 writes a voxel pagoda with thinking on: DFlash2 scored 7, 10 and 9, MTP 0, 0 and 9 (two ran out of the 32k cap). Its thinking budget leaves room for the page; the vLLM entry still runs out.
Unit bakeoff-queue-flash waits for bakeoff-queue-five and then fills Flash-Next (entry flashnext) to five runs of every test; its test 3 runs on Strata because SGLang cannot serve several sessions.
Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B (llama.cpp 0.6, 262k) and Gemma-4-26B-A4B (on trial) are daily drivers 5 and 6. The exllamav3 MTP and DFlash2 entries for Qwen3.8-27B stay in llama-swap.
Test 5 and 6 pages can be reviewed at review.lan.example: each opens in a sandboxed frame inside a script-free viewer page.

Unit bakeoff-queue-five started at 07:24 and is waiting for the GPU lease. It fills Tiel t06, Gemma and Qwen3.8-27B out to five runs after Model Master 2's test 6 releases the card. Phase-d was not restarted.

Phase-d test 2 is still the tree the 16:40 reboot killed (no meta.json, 20 Rust files, 5,267 lines). Test 6 finished at 00:41 and the GPU is free (25 MiB), so only a yes is missing before a rerun. This check did not restart the case.

Night search graded: Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B on llama.cpp 0.6.0 (262k, f16 cache, 149 tok/s short and 98 at 141k) writes the best voxel pagodas (10 and 8, one blank of three); Gemma-4-26B-A4B is fastest (27 s per page, 7, 9 and 0); Qwen3.8-27B with thinking on never finished a page at 32k or 64k.
Test 6 added: a one-shot voxel Japanese pagoda in three.js, graded from frames rendered offline (no-network Chromium, vendored three.js) and the page's console, 0 to 10.

The night search for a 150k-or-more coding setup finished. Six of seven meet the bar; Gemma-4-26B-A4B with MTP is the fastest (267 tok/s on short code, 123 at depth, 262k window). Test 6, the one-shot voxel pagoda, is on its third sitting and was not graded here.

Phase-d test 2 is still the tree the 16:40 reboot killed (no meta.json, 20 Rust files, 5,267 lines). The night search finished and model-master-2 now holds the GPU for test 6 (voxel pagoda), so this check did not restart the case or grade those runs.

Phase-d test 2 is still the tree the 16:40 reboot killed (no meta.json, 20 Rust files, 5,267 lines). model-master-2 holds the GPU since 23:27 for a night search of 150k+ coding setups, with qwen3.8-27b-vllm loaded and the card at 100%, so this check did not restart the case.

Our llama.cpp image (0.6.0, build 11429) runs Qwen3.8-27B with the DFlash2 drafter as a GGUF at 95 / 43 / 108 tok/s (code / prose / structured), no faster than our MTP entry (95 / 63 / 102 in the same sitting), although the drafter is accepted as often as on exllamav3 (47 %). TensorFold in the same sitting 170 / 85 / 213.
llama.cpp + DFlash2 recipe under engines/llamacpp-dflash2 (no new image; drafter GGUF pinned on the NAS). Not a bake-off entry and not in llama-swap. The GPU lease was released at 23:17.

exllamav3 1.6.1 with the DFlash2 drafter writes Qwen3.8-27B at 158 / 73 / 181 tok/s (code / prose / structured) on the RTX 3090, stock and unpatched; TensorFold in the same sitting 170 / 84 / 211; exllamav3 with its own MTP head 116 / 70 / 128. With DFlash2 it holds a 65k window (98k with an 8-bit cache), with MTP 131k. At temperature 0 drafting changes 7 of 15 exllamav3 replies (10 of 15 with MTP); TensorFold's stay identical.

TensorFold 0.6.6 built for the RTX 3090 with a local patch (upstream refuses cards below compute capability 8.9). It is a trial under engines/tensorfold, not a bake-off entry and not in llama-swap. Grok reviewed the patch twice. The GPU lease is released.

Phase-d test 2 is still the tree the 16:40 reboot killed (no meta.json, 20 Rust files, 5,267 lines, last write 16:38). The TensorFold lease is still held, but the card went idle at 25 MiB during this check, so the case was not restarted.

Phase-d test 2 is still the tree the 16:40 reboot killed. It has no meta.json. No bakeoff unit is running. The GPU lease is held by the TensorFold trial, so this check did not restart the case. The graded LFM2.5 test-1 folders were archived and the report rebuilt.

LFM2.5-24B-A2B test 1 graded on both quants with an Opus read of the code. Q4_K_M passes thin: 4 of 5 checks, three read-only commands, 10 of 25. Q6_K fails: it calls API paths the server does not have, 2 of 5 checks, 3 of 25. Both finish in under 2 minutes at 151 to 168 tok/s.
Phase-d test 2 is still the tree the 16:40 reboot killed. It has no meta.json. No bakeoff unit is running. LFM2.5 Q6 now holds the GPU idle, so this check did not restart the case.

LFM2.5 Q6 loaded at 131072 context, but the test did not start. The runner skipped it because the earlier harness failure is still recorded. Q4 failed the same way, from a negative thinking budget at 32k. Neither was graded.
Phase-d test 2 is still the tree the 16:40 reboot killed. It has no meta.json. No bakeoff unit is running, and the GPU is free again. This check did not restart the case.
LFM2.5-24B-A2B Q4_K_M and Q6_K were added on Titan. Both exit before they serve, so nothing was queued. The weights are there. This check did not retry the load.
Saturn rebooted at 16:40 and killed phase-d test 2 about ten minutes before its cap. The case has no meta.json and is not a grade. The model is still loaded and the replay is down.
Phase-d test 2 spent 14:05 to 15:05 in two 30-minute bash timeouts on a mock server, then started the real crate. At 15:35 it had 8 Rust files and 1,837 lines, with the GPU busy. Not graded.

Phase-d test 2 is wedged. Since 14:05 OpenCode has been waiting on a mock python3 server.py (127.0.0.1:8199) whose shell already exited, so the hang watchdog does not fire. The GPU is idle at 22,868 MiB. The 3 h cap is about 16:48. Not graded.
LFM2.5-24B-A2B Q4_K_M finished downloading to the NAS (13.53 GiB). It was not queued. Phase-d still holds the GPU.
the operator asked for LFM2.5-24B-A2B. Q4_K_M (13.53 GiB) is downloading to the NAS. It fits llama.cpp and was not queued. The phase-d case still holds the GPU.
the operator said resume testing. The interrupted phase-d tree was set aside and is not a grade. bakeoff-queue-phased-t2 reruns wb-flashnext-phased only. The llama-swap upgrade was not started.
Titan was down from 07:59 to 11:29. The GPU is idle (lease FREE, 25 MiB). The Qwen3.5-2B baseline did not finish. The bake-off stays paused and did not grade the interrupted phase-d test 2.
Titan stopped answering on the network between 09:34 and 10:32. The bake-off stays paused and did not grade the interrupted phase-d test 2.
Titan does not answer on the network. At 07:29 it was running a Qwen3.5-2B baseline at 100% GPU. The bake-off stays paused and did not grade the interrupted phase-d test 2.

Phase-d test 2 is marked already run in matrix-phased-b-tuned.tsv, so restarting that unit would skip it. The status=ok after the 09:39 cutoff is still not a grade. Titan is still on the same Qwen3.5-4B training from 19:14.
Titan GPU is held by a classifier fine-tune for Qwen3.5-4B training since 19:14, after the Qwen3.5-2B job. The bake-off stays paused. Phase-d test 2 is still not a grade.
Titan GPU is held by a classifier fine-tune for Qwen3.5-2B training since 13:48, after the 0.8B job. The bake-off stays paused. Phase-d test 2 is still not a grade.
Titan GPU is held by the classifier training (Qwen3.5-0.8B) since 10:58. The bake-off stays paused. Phase-d test 2 is still not a grade.

Phase-d test 2 (wb-flashnext-phased) was stopped at 09:39 for the GPU handoff. The harness wrote status=ok after exit 137 and an ALL DONE line at 09:40; that is not a pass and was not graded. Titan is free: lease FREE, nothing running, 25 MiB.

Test 5 orrery is finished, 15 of 15, all status ok. Eight replies contain a parseable SVG. Maya GLM-5.3-Flash hit the length cap and still left a parseable orrery. Phase-d test 2 (wb-flashnext-phased) is running.

Test 5 orrery is 14 of 15 done, all status ok. Qwen3.6-27B, Gemma 4 31B, Gemma 4 26B and Kolibri-1 each stopped with a parseable SVG, so seven of the fourteen replies parse. Maya GLM-5.3-Flash is running; phase-d test 2 still waits.

Test 5 orrery is 10 of 15 done, all status ok. Heretic2 joined Tiel Coder Q4_K_XL and OrcaSAQ-2 with a parseable SVG. Cyber Tiel left a truncated SVG, and plain Tiel Coder hit the length cap with an empty reply. Qwen3.6-27B is running; phase-d test 2 still waits.
The dashboard queue tile now follows the live test-5 log while the wave-B log still ends at ALL DONE, so a refresh no longer shows the queue as idle during the orrery.

Test 5 orrery is 7 of 15 done, all status ok. Only Tiel Coder Q4_K_XL and OrcaSAQ-2 produced a parseable SVG. Three runs hit the length cap with an empty reply, Swift15 hit length with no SVG, and Orcarouter stopped with prose and no SVG. Heretic2 is still loading; phase-d test 2 waits.

Tiel Coder with its MTP draft head, test 2 run 3: the server builds and 20 tests pass, but it flushes stdout only when stdin closes, so a client never sees a reply. Test 2 on that build is one usable server in three. Not a broken tool-call format.
The follow-on is graded. Strata 0.1.42 with the old PCIe share confirmed test 1 at 33.8 tok/s and test 2 at 30.1 tok/s, against 16.8 and 19.2 on the default share. That setting stays.
Strata 0.1.42 with the old PCIe share passed test 2: 9 tools, 77 tests, 61 min, 30.1 tok/s, against 72 tests, 98 min and 19.2 tok/s on the default share.

Tiel Coder with its MTP draft head: test 2 run 1 is partial (invented /api/entities, 29 tests) and run 2 is a thin full pass (5 tools, 9 tests, 81 tok/s). Neither showed a broken tool-call format. Run 3 is still going.

The third Tiel Coder MTP test-1 run also passed (57 tests, 82 tok/s). Grep returned matches and no tool call failed, so drafting has not broken tools on test 1. It is not clearly faster than the plain build.

The Tiel Coder Q4_K_XL focus wave is fully graded (24 of 24). Test 4 passed 9 of 9 with no false done. The write-up is results-wave-b/TIEL-CODER-FOCUS.md: trust it with a small checked patch, not with one MCP server it writes.

Strata 0.1.42 with the old PCIe share passed test 1 at 33.8 tok/s (the default-share run was 16.8). The first two Tiel Coder MTP test-1 runs also passed, at 75 and 67 tok/s; neither called glob or grep.

Six more Tiel Coder test 4 runs passed, including the last bugfix-targets run, so that ticket is 3 of 3. Every hidden check was green and no baseline test regressed. Glob now returns file paths; the old ripgrep unpack error is still gone. Test 4 stays out of the report.
First test 4 case on Tiel Coder Q4_K_XL passed the hidden checks (bugfix-targets, 161 tests, no regressions). Test 4 is not in the report, so the row lives in results-test4/grades.tsv.
A test 2 for the newer SGLang build of Flash-Next is queued last. That build served several sessions at once in a probe; the pick still rests on the older build until this run is graded.
New test 5: one prompt, one reply, an animated SVG of a clockwork orrery; Claude's own answer is kept as the top of the scale. 15 of our models try it after the current queue.
The GPU was lent to another training job at the 18:13 case boundary and came back after 3 minutes because that job failed its own self-test; the Tiel Coder wave went on with test 2T run 2.

The file search tools of the coding agent work now that ripgrep is in the image: in the first three cases graded since the fix the old error is gone and the one grep call made returned its matches. No glob call has been made yet.
The GPU goes to the classifier training after the test-2 repeat now running; the Tiel Coder queue waits and resumes by itself (2 to 5 hours, estimate).
Tiel Coder focus wave started: the Q4_K_XL setup runs every test three times (tests 1, 2, 2T, 3 and 4, 24 cases) for a thorough look at one model.

The coding agent's glob and grep tools never worked in the test sandbox because the image had no ripgrep. It is installed now; earlier runs are not repeated, since every model had the same handicap. Runs from this wave on have working search tools.
The queue is finished and empty. Retry batch 1 and the repeat of the Strata 0.1.42 settings probe are done, the GPU is free, and nothing else is queued.

Strata 0.1.42 settings for Flash-Next, each of five settings measured twice in opposite orders. Going back to the older PCIe share was the best single change: about 152 seconds per probe against 188 with the release defaults, long answers at about 95 tok/s against 48, and a large prompt read at about 2,000 tok/s against 1,200. Turning tail skip off decodes as fast but does not help reading. Everything ran faster in the second round, so smaller differences are noise.

The file search tools of the coding agent (glob and grep) have failed inside the test sandbox since at least 2026-10-01: the agent image lacks ripgrep and the fallback download cannot be unpacked there. 57 of 181 runs asked for them and got an error, the reference runs included; the models fell back to shell commands. Not fixed yet, so the running wave stays comparable.

Test 3 now credits a right value even when the model wrote its answer file in its own layout. Four runs gain: OrcaSAQ-2-Cyber and Gemma 4 31B on the known-good server go from 0 to 14 of 14 facts, Coder390 from 6 to 14 on the known-good server and from 1 to 6 on its own. Every recovered value was checked by hand.

Test 3 now also puts its task text in a file in the work folder, because models that compacted their conversation lost the required answer layout. Runs from today on are not strictly comparable with the 35 earlier ones.

A repeat of the Strata 0.1.42 settings probe is queued behind the retry runs: one warm-up that is not counted, then each of the five settings twice, in opposite orders. In the first probe the opening run was a cold start, so the settings could not be ranked.

Three grading questions are settled. Test 3 will also give its task as a file, and runs that missed only on answer layout will be regraded. Test 1 keeps counting an explicit nothing-matched message with exit code 0 as clean handling of bad input. Test 2 keeps grading the server's main read tool; another working tool does not turn a partial into a pass.

The newer SGLang build for Flash-Next (phase-d-main) served several sessions at once in a probe, 11 of 11 checks, which the older build could not. In test 1 it passed 5 of 5 at 25.3 tok/s; the older build ran at 44.3 tok/s on 2026-10-01 under earlier harness settings, so the two speeds are not directly comparable.

Claw took over the hourly check and the daily Iris check from the Saturn session. Public model cards now wait for the operator's yes before they are pushed, and the published report is updated only when someone republishes it.
The hourly check and the daily Iris check of the Saturn session were stopped for the handover to Claw. The queue keeps running, and new results wait ungraded until the new schedule starts.

The SGLang phase-d check did not run at 09:30: the settings sync stopped because the Strata probe's settings file was already in the repo before its entry existed on Titan. It is queued again to run right after the Strata settings probe, still ahead of the five retry test-2 runs.
Every model entry's settings file is now also copied to a folder on Titan that the llama-watch dashboard can read, with the model's record included, so the dashboard can show per-model settings.

Added a settings probe for Strata 0.1.42 on Flash-Next after the SGLang check: six variants on one fixed workload, each new setting switched separately. The server logs show the new defaults read prompts more slowly on Titan (45 to 61 tok/s on small additions against 72 with the older settings).
Added a check of the SGLang fork's newer phase-d-main build for Flash-Next: a multi-session probe and a test-1 run, right after the Strata 0.1.42 test 2 and ahead of the retry test-2 runs.
